joshua.9.p1.b1.text: Now when news of this reached all the kings west of the Jordan—those in the hill country, the foothills … they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.

joshua.9.p1.b2.text: But the people of Gibeon, having heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, acted deceptively and set out as envoys,

joshua.9.p1.b3.text: … their whole supply of bread was dry and moldy.

joshua.9.p1.b4.text: carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended. They put worn, patched sandals on their feet and threadbare clothing on their bodies …

joshua.9.p2.b1.text: They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal …

joshua.9.p2.b2.text: “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”

joshua.9.p2.b3.text: “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?”

joshua.9.p2.b4.text: “Who are you and where have you come from?”

joshua.9.p2.b5.text: “Your servants have come from a very distant land … because of the fame of the LORD your God …

joshua.9.p3.b1.text: “This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But take a look, it is now dry and moldy.

joshua.9.p3.b2.text: These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they are cracked …

joshua.9.p3.b3.text: Then the men of Israel sampled their provisions, but did not seek the counsel of the LORD.

joshua.9.p3.b4.text: And Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.

joshua.9.p4.b1.text: Three days after they had made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites learned that they were neighbors, living among them.

joshua.9.p4.b2.text: So the Israelites set out and on the third day arrived at their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

joshua.9.p4.b3.text: … And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.

joshua.9.p4.b4.text: “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.

joshua.9.p4.b5.text: … let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” So the leaders kept their promise.

joshua.9.p5.b1.text: “Why did you deceive us by telling us you live far away from us, when in fact you live among us?

joshua.9.p5.b2.text: … you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”

joshua.9.p5.b3.text: … So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.

joshua.9.p5.b4.text: Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”

joshua.9.p6.b1.text: So Joshua did this and delivered them from the hands of the Israelites …

joshua.9.p6.b2.text: On that day he made them woodcutters and water carriers, as they are to this day for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose.
